excerpt: Pilot provides bookkeeping, tax and CFO services for startups and small businesses, combining in-house software with US-based finance experts. Bookkeeping starts at $99/month; valued at $1.2B in 2021.
content:
Pilot runs the financial back office for startups and small businesses. Instead of hiring an in-house bookkeeper or a local accountant, a company connects its bank, card, payroll and payment accounts to Pilot, and Pilot's team uses its own software to categorise transactions, reconcile accounts and close the books each month. Customers can add tax preparation, CFO services such as budgeting and investor reporting, and COO services. Pilot's About page says it gives customers a team of finance experts who take this work off their plate. It also states that Pilot is not a public accounting firm and does not provide services that require a licence to practise public accountancy.

Pilot was founded by Waseem Daher (CEO), Jessica McKellar (CTO) and Jeff Arnold (COO). TechCrunch reported in March 2018 that the three had earlier built Ksplice, which let administrators apply security patches without rebooting and was sold to Oracle in 2011, and that Pilot launched with $15 million in funding led by Index Ventures. In March 2021 CNBC reported that Pilot raised a $100 million round led by Bezos Expeditions, Jeff Bezos's investment firm, and the hedge fund Whale Rock Capital, with Sequoia and Index Ventures joining, which doubled its valuation to $1.2 billion. Stripe and its founders had invested earlier. Pilot's About page says it has raised more than $150 million in total and lists offices in San Francisco and Nashville.

Pilot publishes its prices. The Essentials bookkeeping plan costs $99 a month for businesses with up to $100,000 in monthly expenses and uses AI to categorise transactions, reconcile accounts and close the books monthly, with support through in-app messaging. Higher tiers add a dedicated US-based bookkeeper, accrual accounting, bill management and custom reporting, and are priced by monthly expenses. Tax, CFO and COO services are priced separately on the same page, and a free trial is offered.

This profile draws on Pilot's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the service, and nothing here is paid placement.
